title: Local finite free scalar Hom cohomology
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ any open subscheme, $K$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $E$ an integer-indexed cochain complex of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Suppose $E^p=0$ for all sufficiently large $p$ and every $E^p$ is isomorphic to a finite sum of copies of $\mathcal O_U$, allowing rank zero. Suppose $\epsilon:E\to (K|_U)[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For any supplied derived-category universe on $Y$ [def-pc-derived-category] and any $q\in\mathbf Z$, put $F^q=H^q(R\mathcal Hom_Y(K,\mathcal O_Y))$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $F^q$ restricted to the over-$U$ module site is isomorphic to the inverse image under the over-site equivalence of $H^q(\mathcal Hom_U^\bullet(E,\mathcal O_U[0]))$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. No affine, regularity, closed-immersion or derived-universe hypothesis on $U$ is required.

source.place: Tag 08DL, open restriction; Tag 08DM applied degreewise to bounded truncations; existing bounded-above finite-free Hom model

proof.text: Compute ambient derived Hom using a bounded-below injective resolution I (hence K-injective) of the degree-zero structure sheaf. The representative theorem and homology factorization identify its cohomology with the Hom complex of single K and I; exact restriction commutes with homology.

Restriction preserves K-injectives and commutes with the ordinary Hom complex; transport via the equivalence between the over-U site and U.toScheme. The equivalence restricts local module morphisms and preserves their products and compositions, hence the Hom differential.

In the standard derived universe on U.toScheme, apply the bounded-above finite-free model to E, its augmentation and the degree-zero unit complex. The target is bounded below by zero. Taking homology identifies its Hom complex with the restricted derived Hom from the preceding step. For each fixed homology degree, boundedness below of I allows truncating the bounded-above finite free E far enough to apply the strictly perfect comparison of Tag 08DM; no lower bound on E is assumed.

The representative comparison in both derived universes uses the same ambient I and ordinary Hom complex. Compose the homology isomorphisms and return through the over-site equivalence. This removes the need for a localization on U in the supplied universe.

theorem local_finite_free_scalar_homology
    {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (U : Y.Opens) (K : Y.Modules)
    (E : CochainComplex U.toScheme.Modules ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ p : ℤ, N < p → IsZero (E.X p))
    (hfree : ∀ p : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (E.X p ≅
      SheafOfModules.free (R := moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)
        (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))
    (ε : E ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor U.toScheme.Modules 0).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj K)) [QuasiIso ε] (q : ℤ) :
    let F : Y.Modules := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) q).obj
        ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
          (op ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj K),
            (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
                (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf)))
    Nonempty (F.over U ≅ (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U).inverse.obj
      ((homComplex (R := U.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf) E
        ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor U.toScheme.Modules 0).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf))).homology q))
